articles.title: US-Canada trade war deepens, raising costs on both sides
articles.titleCn: 美加贸易战升级，双方成本上升
articles.summary: Canada is on Tuesday set to announce its response to new tariffs imposed by US President Donald Trump, as the two neighbors and former close allies become embroiled in a trade war.
articles.summaryCn: 美加贸易战加剧，加拿大宣布报复性关税，双方经济成本上升，专家称无人受益。

Canada is set to announce its response on Tuesday to new tariffs imposed by US President Donald Trump, as the two neighbors and former close allies become {{0}} in a trade war. The Canadian government said late on Monday that the ministers of finance, industry and labor, along with other senior officials, would hold a press conference in Ottawa to {{1}} Canada's response to "these challenging times."
Trump said on Monday that tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks and auto parts would rise from 25% to 50% starting January 1, 2027. A 50% US tariff on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, including hockey sticks and cement, took effect just after midnight on Saturday, after extended trade negotiations collapsed. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney earlier said {{2}} tariffs would take effect starting September 8 on US imports like steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, paper and electronics. Carney said on Monday that Ottawa would be willing to talk if Washington changed tack.

articles.fullText:
Canada is set to announce its response on Tuesday to new tariffs imposed by US President Donald Trump, as the two neighbors and former close allies become embroiled in a trade war.
The Canadian government said late on Monday that the ministers of finance, industry and labor, along with other senior officials, would hold a press conference in Ottawa to outline Canada's response to "these challenging times."
Trump said on Monday that tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks and auto parts would rise from 25% to 50% starting January 1, 2027.
A 50% US tariff on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, including hockey sticks and cement, took effect just after midnight on Saturday, after extended trade negotiations collapsed. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney earlier said retaliatory tariffs would take effect starting September 8 on US imports like steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, paper and electronics.
Carney said on Monday that Ottawa would be willing to talk if Washington changed tack. "When the Americans go to the negotiating table first, with the right attitude toward our industries and in a true partnership, of course we'll come to the negotiating table," he said.
He added that he would not accept the attitude that "Canada is a subsidiary of the United States," or that the country should be disadvantaged relative to the US.
Hockey sticks are seen in a store in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, August 23, 2026. 
'Enough is enough'
Other Canadian political leaders joined Carney and stepped up their rhetoric on Monday in response to the latest US tariff threats.
Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne urged a firm stance during consultations in Montreal. "At some point you have to say enough is enough," Champagne said, indicating that federal support is on the way for businesses hit by 50% tariffs.
Champagne emphasized ongoing work to build a resilient economy, stating, "Plan A has always been to build a strong Canadian economy, to remove interprovincial trade barriers, to diversify our economy and to do big things in our country."
Former Prime Minister Jean Chretien urged Ottawa to hit back with export taxes on critical commodities such as energy, oil, natural gas and potash. "If we want to stay upright, we have to hit where it hurts," Chretien said. "That's where we should tax. The advantage of an export tax is it's not us who pays, it's the Americans."
Ontario Premier Doug Ford also took an assertive stance, calling for all available countermeasures to be deployed. Ford warned that Canada must be ready to cut off electricity and critical mineral exports to the United States if trade relations worsen.
"I'll cut them off," Ford said regarding mineral shipments. "You won't get a grain of sand out of Ontario."
Economic interdependence
Public opinion appears to be backing Ottawa's tougher stance, even as concerns over the economic fallout grow.
Three in four Canadians support the Carney government's decision to walk away from trade talks, according to a poll released on Sunday by the Angus Reid Institute. Meanwhile, two in five Canadians said they feared for their jobs.
Those concerns reflect economic interdependence between Canada and the US. Canadian exports to the US account for about 70% of the country's total exports, while Canada is the US' second-largest goods trading partner this year and its largest foreign supplier of energy, according to Canadian government data.
Canada supplies the vast majority of US natural gas and electricity imports, as well as about 60% of US crude oil imports, Carney said.
"I don't think they want us to stop sending any of that energy," he said.
Canada is also a major supplier of commodities such as potash, for which it is the world's largest producer, as well as critical minerals including lithium, nickel and graphite.
The auto industry is particularly important to Ontario, the center of Canada's vehicle manufacturing sector. Automakers and suppliers on both sides of the border are deeply integrated, with auto parts routinely crossing the US-Canada border multiple times during production.
Ford, General Motors and Stellantis operate major assembly plants in Ontario, while the broader supply chain supports tens of thousands of jobs.
Spools of steel in the yard at an ArcelorMittal Dofasco facility in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, August 20, 2026. 
No winners in trade war
The growing tariff confrontation is likely to hurt businesses and consumers in both countries, experts say, as higher tariffs raise production costs and ultimately push up prices.
British Columbia Premier David Eby told CNN on Monday that US consumers would feel the impact across a wide range of products, from plywood and flooring materials to cut flowers and fishing equipment.
"It is a bizarre policy for Americans. It's going to hurt them," he said.
Trade policy analyst Deborah Elms from the Hinrich Foundation told CNA that ultimately, nobody wins in a tit-for-tat tariff war.
"Canadian tariffs will be paid by Americans and American companies importing from Canada. So, they're going to hit Americans rather than Canadians," she said.
"And Canada will have a much harder time exporting to the US at 50% tariffs. That completely ruins profit margins. If Canada retaliates, (there'll be) additional pain on Canadians who are trying to import goods from the US," Elms said.

articles.title: English hospitals aim to ramp up use of robotics in surgery
articles.titleCn: 英国医院计划加大机器人手术应用力度
articles.summary: The UK government has announced plans to invest more in robotic equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of keyhole surgeries carried out in England by 2035
articles.summaryCn: 英国政府计划到2035年使90%的微创手术使用机器人辅助，以提升手术精准度、缩短恢复时间并缓解医疗系统压力。

paragraphs.en:
The UK government has announced plans to invest more in {{1}} equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of {{2}} surgeries carried out in England by 2035. The government highlighted robotics as one of five "big bets" in a 10-year health plan for England, alongside other {{3}} technologies: data, AI, {{4}} and {{5}}. Surgeons and nurses using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing surgery, at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
At St Bartholomew's Hospital in central London, visiting surgeons are among the first to be trained to use the new da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, made by US company Initiative. The system, which includes three robotic arms that can hold surgical equipment, is controlled using an {{6}} 3D headset and a video-game-like {{7}}.
paragraphs.cn: 英国政府宣布计划增加对英格兰医院机器人设备的投资，并设定目标，到2035年英格兰90%的微创手术将使用机器人辅助。政府将机器人技术列为英格兰十年健康计划中的五大“重大赌注”之一，其他变革性技术包括数据、人工智能、基因组学和可穿戴设备。外科医生和护士在伦敦圣巴塞洛缪医院使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

paragraphs.en:
Robotic surgical systems like this can be used across a range of {{8}} including {{9}}, {{10}}, {{11}}, {{12}}, and {{13}} or general surgery. Sasha Stamenkovic (C) using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing lung cancer surgery as Ali Ansaripour (R), senior cardiothoracic trainee on a robotic fellowship, looks on. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
The {{14}} of robotic-assisted surgery should mean shorter hospital stays and quicker recovery times, which will take {{15}} off a struggling health service with year-long waitlists, workforce shortages and discharge {{16}}. "The ability to have lots of {{17}} computer-aided technology on top" of human-controlled robotics "makes this precise surgery. It makes it safe surgery," says Sasha Stamenkovic, Director of Robotic Surgery and Research at Barts Health NHS Trust.
paragraphs.cn: 在伦敦市中心的圣巴塞洛缪医院，来访的外科医生是首批接受培训使用美国公司Initiative制造的新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统的人。该系统包括三个可持手术器械的机械臂，通过沉浸式3D头显和类似视频游戏的控制台进行操作。

paragraphs.en:
As well as improving recovery times, the greater precision also reduces the risk of {{18}} like air leaks, a common cause of longer hospital stays following lung surgery. articles.fullText:
The UK government has announced plans to invest more in robotic equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of keyhole surgeries carried out in England by 2035.
The government highlighted robotics as one of five "big bets" in a 10-year health plan for England, alongside other transformative technologies: data, AI, genomics and wearables.
Surgeons and nurses using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing surgery, at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
At St Bartholomew's Hospital in central London, visiting surgeons are among the first to be trained to use the new da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, made by US company Initiative. The system, which includes three robotic arms that can hold surgical equipment, is controlled using an immersive 3D headset and a video-game-like console.
Robotic surgical systems like this can be used across a range of specialties including urology, gynecology, abdominal, colorectal, and thoracic or general surgery.
Sasha Stamenkovic (C) using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing lung cancer surgery as Ali Ansaripour (R), senior cardiothoracic trainee on a robotic fellowship, looks on. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
The precision of robotic-assisted surgery should mean shorter hospital stays and quicker recovery times, which will take strain off a struggling health service with year-long waitlists, workforce shortages and discharge bottlenecks.
"The ability to have lots of integrated computer-aided technology on top" of human-controlled robotics "makes this precise surgery. It makes it safe surgery," says Sasha Stamenkovic, Director of Robotic Surgery and Research at Barts Health NHS Trust.
As well as improving recovery times, the greater precision also reduces the risk of complications like air leaks, a common cause of longer hospital stays following lung surgery.
Nurses assisting in lung cancer surgery using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, at St Bartholomew's Hospital. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
Ian Macleod was the first patient in Britain's NHS to undergo lung cancer surgery using the new da Vinci robotic system. Macleod says he "didn't realize" until he was wearing a surgical gown and anesthetised that he would hold this groundbreaking title, but the news "didn't faze" the 76-year-old retired detective.
Thirty minutes after the robotic-assisted operation, Macleod was back on his feet. "It was extraordinary," he says. "In fact, after the operation, I found out quite quickly that I only had one stitch." He had undergone non-robotic keyhole surgery for a different cancer in the past, and says the recovery time was "much longer". This time, he was driving his wife to the garden centrer for coffee less than a week later.
Stamenkovic runs fellowships at St Bartholomew's training surgeons on this new technology. He says it is the young surgeons who pick up the new robotic control system the fastest and who become the most adept.
"They've come with different skill sets," he says, "they've probably come with gaming skill sets, some of them have come with a musical background."
Laying out his long-term mission, Stamenkovic added: "All we need to do is harness their energy, their passion, their skill set, and teach them the right moves. And that will make the surgeon of the future."
articles.fullTextCn:
英国政府宣布计划增加对英格兰医院机器人设备的投资，并设定目标，到2035年英格兰90%的微创手术将使用机器人辅助。政府将机器人技术列为英格兰十年健康计划中的五大“重大赌注”之一，其他变革性技术包括数据、人工智能、基因组学和可穿戴设备。外科医生和护士在伦敦圣巴塞洛缪医院使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

在伦敦市中心的圣巴塞洛缪医院，来访的外科医生是首批接受培训使用美国公司Initiative制造的新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统的人。该系统包括三个可持手术器械的机械臂，通过沉浸式3D头显和类似视频游戏的控制台进行操作。

此类机器人手术系统可应用于多个专科，包括泌尿科、妇科、腹部、结直肠、胸外科或普外科。Sasha Stamenkovic（中）使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行肺癌手术，Ali Ansaripour（右）是机器人专科的高级心胸外科培训生，正在旁观看。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

机器人辅助手术的精准性应能缩短住院时间和加快恢复速度，这将缓解一个面临漫长等待名单、劳动力短缺和出院瓶颈的艰难医疗系统的压力。“在人类控制的机器人技术之上集成大量计算机辅助技术的能力，使这种手术精准、安全，”巴特斯健康NHS信托机器人手术与研究主任Sasha Stamenkovic说。

除了改善恢复时间，更高的精准度还降低了并发症风险，如肺手术后常见的导致住院时间延长的漏气问题。护士在圣巴塞洛缪医院使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统协助肺癌手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

Ian Macleod是英国NHS中第一位使用新型达芬奇机器人系统进行肺癌手术的患者。Macleod说，直到穿上手术服并被麻醉时，他才意识到自己将拥有这一开创性的头衔，但这一消息“没有吓到”这位76岁的退休侦探。机器人辅助手术后30分钟，Macleod就能重新站起来。

“这太不可思议了，”他说。“事实上，手术后我很快发现只有一针缝合。”他过去曾因另一种癌症接受过非机器人微创手术，并表示恢复时间“长得多”。这次，不到一周后，他就开车带妻子去花园中心喝咖啡。Stamenkovic在圣巴塞洛缪医院开展专科培训，教授外科医生这项新技术。他说，年轻外科医生掌握新机器人控制系统最快，也最熟练。

“他们带来了不同的技能组合，”他说，“他们可能带来了游戏技能，有些人有音乐背景。”Stamenkovic阐述他的长期使命时说：“我们所要做的就是利用他们的能量、热情和技能，教他们正确的动作。这将造就未来的外科医生。”

articles.fullText:
Europe is experiencing a summer of extreme heat and drought, with record temperatures, wildfire risks and falling river levels affecting several countries.
A scorched landscape in the wake of a wildfire that swept through the Gironde region in Lege-Cap-Ferret, southwestern France, August 4, 2026. 
France recorded its hottest July since nationwide records began in 1900, with a monthly average temperature of 24.9 degrees Celsius, according to Meteo-France.
Rainfall across the country was nearly 70% below the seasonal average, making July 2026 the third-driest July on record.
Persistent heat, drought and windy conditions kept wildfire risks high or very high, while a wildfire in the southwestern department of Gironde burned about 42,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of more than 220,000 people.
Boats lie in the dried out riverbed of a branch of the river Danube in Hainburg, Austria, August 3, 2026. 
In Austria, a national temperature record of 41 degrees Celsius was set on Tuesday as the heat wave continued. The record was measured in the Stammersdorf region of Vienna, according to Austria's state broadcaster ORF.
A forest fire is also raging in Burgenland, while the Lobau wetlands in Vienna face the highest fire danger level. Meanwhile, water levels on the Danube River have fallen to historically low levels, comparable to the major low-water years of 2003 and 2018.
The dried-up Danube riverbed with the Paks power plant at the background, near Dunaszentbenedek, close to Paks town, Hungary, July 31, 2026. 
Neighboring Hungary has extended its highest-level heat alert until midnight on Friday as forecasts show the heat wave will continue. Authorities warned that persistent high temperatures could affect everyone and urged people to take precautions.
The heat wave has intensified drought conditions, lowered water levels in major rivers and increased wildfire risks, with firefighters recently responding to around 100 outdoor fires per day.
A firefighting helicopter flies toward a wildfire on a mountain near L'Aquila, central Italy, August 3, 2026. 
Italy is also facing its fourth major heat wave of the summer, with temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius in some areas.
The Health Ministry placed 25 of the country's 27 monitored cities under the highest heat alert, including Rome, Milan, Florence, Bologna, Venice, Naples and Palermo.
Hot and dry conditions have increased wildfire risks and put pressure on agriculture, with farmers reporting reduced crop yields and higher irrigation demand.
A general view of the Paks nuclear power plant, Hungary, July 31, 2026. 
Low river levels and rising water temperatures have also affected nuclear power operations in parts of Europe.
Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant, which supplies nearly half of the country's electricity, remained operational but its operation depended on river conditions and cooling system performance.
Romania's Cernavoda nuclear power plant shut down both reactors after low Danube water levels affected operations. In France and Switzerland, some nuclear facilities also faced operational disruptions as high river temperatures affected cooling capacity.
The combination of extreme heat, drought and declining water availability is putting pressure on public health, agriculture, wildfire prevention and energy systems in affected areas.

articles.title: UN launches $22m education initiative for Sudan's children
articles.titleCn: 联合国发起2200万美元教育倡议，援助苏丹儿童
articles.summary: The support will benefit children in three Sudanese states; West Darfur, South Kordofan and Gedaref with the aim of restoring “safe, quality and inclusive education” amid the world's largest humanitarian and displacement crisis.
articles.summaryCn: 联合国教育基金启动2200万美元项目，旨在帮助苏丹近20万名受冲突影响的儿童恢复教育。

paragraphs.en:
Sudan's {{0}} conflict has kept millions of children out of school, {{1}} their education and leaving many without a safe place to learn. According to Education Cannot Wait, the UN's global fund for education, at least eight million children nearly half of Sudan's 17 million school-age children are still out of school. "Across the country, large numbers of schools remain {{2}}, while millions of children have {{3}} prolonged {{4}} to their education, with some missing nearly 500 days of learning," the organization stressed. Displaced Sudanese students attend a class at an elementary school run by the Sudanese Coalition for Education in partnership with the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (UNICEF), south of Port Sudan, April 26, 2026. /CFP
In response, the UN's global fund for education in crises, has announced a $22 million program aimed at helping nearly 200,000 children and adolescents affected by the conflict {{5}} their education.

苏丹的长期冲突使数百万儿童失学，扰乱了他们的教育，使许多儿童没有安全的学习场所。据联合国全球教育基金“教育不能等待”称，至少有800万儿童——约占苏丹1700万学龄儿童的一半——仍然失学。该组织强调：“全国范围内，大量学校仍无法运作，而数百万儿童的教育遭受长期中断，有些儿童缺失了近500天的学习时间。”2026年4月26日，在苏丹港以南，流离失所的苏丹学生参加由苏丹教育联盟与联合国儿童基金会合作开办的一所小学的课程。/CFP

"This investment is about much more than reopening classrooms. It is about supporting children to {{9}} a sense of safety and {{10}} while {{11}} education systems that can continue serving communities through crisis and into recovery,”Maysa Jalbout, Director of Education Cannot Wait said. The three-year program will target children most affected by the conflict, including internally displaced children, refugees and {{13}} host communities. At least 60% of {{12}} will be girls and 10% children with disabilities.
paragraphs.cn: 这项支持将惠及苏丹三个州的儿童：西达尔富尔、南科尔多凡和加达里夫，旨在在全球最大的人道主义和流离失所危机中恢复“安全、优质和包容的教育”。“这项投资不仅仅是重新开放教室，而是支持儿童重获安全感和正常感，同时加强教育系统，使其能够在危机期间和恢复过程中继续服务社区，”教育不能等待主任梅萨·贾尔布特表示。这项为期三年的计划将针对受冲突影响最严重的儿童，包括境内流离失所儿童、难民和脆弱的收容社区。至少60%的受益者将是女孩，10%将是残疾儿童。

articles.fullText:
Sudan's prolonged conflict has kept millions of children out of school, disrupting their education and leaving many without a safe place to learn.
According to Education Cannot Wait, the UN's global fund for education, at least eight million children nearly half of Sudan's 17 million school-age children are still out of school.
"Across the country, large numbers of schools remain non-operational, while millions of children have endured prolonged disruptions to their education, with some missing nearly 500 days of learning," the organization stressed.
Displaced Sudanese students attend a class at an elementary school run by the Sudanese Coalition for Education in partnership with the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (UNICEF), south of Port Sudan, April 26, 2026. /CFP
In response, the UN's global fund for education in crises, has announced a $22 million program aimed at helping nearly 200,000 children and adolescents affected by the conflict resume their education.
The support will benefit children in three Sudanese states; West Darfur, South Kordofan and Gedaref with the aim of restoring "safe, quality and inclusive education" amid the world's largest humanitarian and displacement crisis.
"This investment is about much more than reopening classrooms. It is about supporting children to regain a sense of safety and normalcy while strengthening education systems that can continue serving communities through crisis and into recovery,”Maysa Jalbout, Director of Education Cannot Wait said.
The three-year program will target children most affected by the conflict, including internally displaced children, refugees and vulnerable host communities. At least 60% of beneficiaries will be girls and 10% children with disabilities.
Sudanese refugee students take the Grade 8 national examination inside a classroom at a school at the Ura Refugee Site in Asosa Zone, Benishangul-Gumuz region, Ethiopia, June 19, 2026. /CFP
The initiative will create safer learning environments, provide mental health and psychosocial support, strengthen teacher capacity and improve access to learning materials. It will also seek to remove barriers preventing girls and children with disabilities from attending school.
According to UNICEF's mid-year update on Sudan, 81% of schools in Darfur remain closed, while 70% of children in the region are not attending school. Another 5.8% of schools are being used as shelters.
The Sudan initiative comes as Education Cannot Wait launches its "Hope Starts Here" global campaign, seeking to raise $600 million to support 10 million children whose education has been disrupted by some of the world's most severe crises.

articles.fullText:
Israeli air strikes and gunfire killed two young children and at least two other Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on Monday, health officials in the territory said.
Medics and relatives said 10-year-old Amal Abu Khater was hit by a bullet in her back while she was eating inside her family's tent in the enclave's southern city of Khan Younis. The fire came from Israeli forces to the east, they added.
The Israeli military said it was not aware of any incident involving a 10-year-old girl.
A four-year-old boy and another Palestinian were killed in separate Israeli air strikes on a house in Bureij refugee camp and a road in Khan Younis, medics said.
Earlier on Monday, another Israeli air strike killed one person and wounded another at a tent in Deir Al-Balah in the central Gaza Strip, medics said.
The Israeli military said that the strike in Deir Al-Balah targeted a Hamas militant, but did not specifically respond to questions about the other two reported attacks in Khan Younis and Bureij.
The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said three UN warehouses in Deir al-Balah were damaged in an air strike on an adjacent location. All three sustained damage, one of them significantly.
"Civilians and civilian objects, including humanitarian facilities, must always be protected," the office said.
The Israeli military and the Shin Bet domestic security agency struck two mosques in the Gaza Strip on Monday, alleging that Hamas was using the sites to store weapons, according to a joint statement issued by the military and the agency.
The strikes were conducted in the Shati and Deir al-Balah areas in the strip, dismantling two "Hamas weapons storage facilities," containing dozens of Kalashnikov rifles and additional military equipment, the statement said.
It alleged that Hamas used these facilities inside the mosques to conceal and store weapons.
UN humanitarians said on Monday that partners reported deadly weekend airstrikes in Gaza and clashes in the West Bank claimed civilian lives.
In the West Bank, OCHA said that Israeli forces shot and killed another child in Askar Camp in the Nablus governorate, during a raid where local partners and medical sources reported that Palestinians threw stones and Israeli forces fired live ammunition and tear gas canisters.
The office said that in the Silwan area of East Jerusalem, three Palestinians were killed and others were injured on Sunday during a family dispute. Humanitarian partners said that two of them were killed by Israeli forces who raided the neighborhood to intervene and reportedly fired live ammunition and tear gas canisters.

加沙地带卫生官员称，以色列周一在该地区的空袭和枪击造成两名幼童和至少另外两名巴勒斯坦人死亡。医务人员和亲属表示，10岁的阿迈勒·阿布·哈特尔在位于飞地南部城市汗尤尼斯的家中帐篷内吃饭时，背部中弹。他们补充说，枪火来自东部的以色列军队。以色列军方表示，不知道任何涉及一名10岁女孩的事件。医务人员称，一名四岁男孩和另一名巴勒斯坦人在以色列对布赖杰难民营的一所房屋和汗尤尼斯的一条道路的单独空袭中丧生。

周一早些时候，医务人员称，以色列另一次空袭在加沙地带中部的代尔巴拉的一顶帐篷处打死一人，打伤另一人。以色列军方表示，对代尔巴拉的空袭目标是哈马斯武装分子，但没有具体回应关于汗尤尼斯和布赖杰的另外两起报告的袭击的问题。联合国人道主义事务协调厅表示，代尔巴拉的三处联合国仓库在一次对邻近地点的空袭中受损。三处均受损，其中一处受损严重。该办公室表示：“平民和平民物体，包括人道设施，必须始终受到保护。”

根据军方和国内安全机构辛贝特发布的联合声明，以色列军方和辛贝特周一袭击了加沙地带的两座清真寺，声称哈马斯利用这些地点储存武器。声明称，袭击在加沙地带的沙提和代尔巴拉地区进行，摧毁了两个“哈马斯武器储存设施”，其中包含数十支卡拉什尼科夫步枪和额外的军事装备。声明称，哈马斯利用清真寺内的这些设施隐藏和储存武器。联合国人道机构周一表示，合作伙伴报告称，周末加沙的致命空袭和约旦河西岸的冲突夺走了平民生命。在约旦河西岸，人道协调厅表示，以色列军队在纳布卢斯省的阿斯卡难民营的一次突袭中开枪打死另一名儿童，当地合作伙伴和医疗消息来源称，巴勒斯坦人投掷石块，以色列军队发射实弹和催泪瓦斯罐。

该办公室表示，在东耶路撒冷的西尔万地区，周日发生家庭纠纷，三名巴勒斯坦人被打死，另有数人受伤。人道合作伙伴表示，其中两人是被以色列军队打死的，这些军队突袭该社区进行干预，据报道发射了实弹和催泪瓦斯罐。
